sentence: This project studies how protein neddylation protects the function of the endothelium and its cells in vascular disease.
This project studies the fungi that cause mucormycosis and the host factors that help the disease develop.
This project builds spatial transcriptomics tools and computational methods to study how immune cells and pathogens interact in tissues.
This project tests whether a microRNA predicts and causes bronchopulmonary dysplasia in premature babies by reducing lung blood vessels.
This project studies how a calcium channel in the urothelium affects the bladder's storage and voiding functions.
This project builds a shared platform that uses standardized assays to study how cancer patients respond to immunotherapy in clinical trials.
This project tests a cancer treatment that targets the metabolism of fibrolamellar hepatocellular carcinoma tumors, combined with treatments that work on the immune system.
This project builds a web platform that lets users analyze and view cancer regulatory genomics and chromatin structure using genomic data.
This project studies how communication between organs keeps tissue stem cells working, using transcription factors and stem cells in the fruit fly ovary.
This project builds a mechanical testing tool to study the mechanics of solid tumors.
This project builds a collapsible vaginal pessary and applicator for treating pelvic organ prolapse without surgery.
This project studies whether heart conditions that cause clotting are linked to central retinal artery occlusion, a type of stroke in the eye.
This project studies how T-cells activated during heart failure harm heart function through gap junctions with cardiomyocytes.
This project studies how microRNAs change cardiac ion channels through a biophysical action separate from RNA interference, using transgenic mice.
This project supports discoveries that help diagnose and treat cancer.
This project uses structural approaches to study how megalin, a protein, recycles between the cell surface and compartments inside the cell.
This project tests and improves a drug that breaks down the androgen receptor protein as a treatment for spinobulbar muscular atrophy.
This project uses metabolomics and computational methods to work out how compounds against Mycobacterium tuberculosis work.
This project studies how two proteins help endothelial cells that line blood and lymphatic vessels sense the forces of circulatory flow.
This project uses interviews to find the concerns of sexual and gender minority cancer patients and tests methods to include them in studies.
